source_title: Could aviation at last be close to earning its wings?
business_context: Which airline performance cohorts create or destroy economic profit?
key_message: Among 97 airlines in 2025, the top 20 created +$14bn, the middle 57 lost $2.3bn, and the bottom 20 lost $22.9bn; concentration of losses matters more than industry-average direction.

data_spec.difference_explanation: not disclosed; different scope possible, not assumed

data_recipe: calculate per-company economic profit (ROIC minus WACC times invested capital)
separately verify coverage of industry-level aggregate
render left negative, right positive bars
message_conditions: consistent measurement year and USD units
cohort total not mean per airline
diff_notes: Original Exhibit 2 SVGZ image inaccessible. Chart is editorial cohort-summary bars rather than original power curve. Source group amounts do not reconcile with article industry total.

training_pair.instruction: Use reported airline cohort totals to construct an editable diverging bar chart of economic-profit asymmetry.
training_pair.response: Use bundled chart.py render(data,theme,context)->fig and data.csv (top,+14.0,20; middle,-2.3,57; bottom,-22.9,20; year 2025; USD billions). config.json THEME.source/neutral, CONTEXT labels. Run python chart.py --data data.csv --config config.json --theme source --output source.png. Do not present as McKinsey source power curve; group sum -11.2 != published industry -12.8.
